Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then use the wake-visual-signals skill to inspect the required rollout keyframes before touching the target policy. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and won’t consult the omitted research shelf or neighboring history.

The skill requires a score-anchored comparison of the common prewarm state and at least two rollout keyframe sheets. I’m now inventorying the assigned guidance, sampled policies, metrics, and inherited optimizer notes so the diagnosis can be evidence-backed before any edit.

The evidence now isolates two distinct late-mode findings: a modest opposite bearing fraction (`-0.25`) is the best sampled continuation and preserves the useful upstream leg, while the inherited full-circle `atan` reconstruction catastrophically destroys that leg (`-0.57L` head-x, `9.27L` closest range). I’m inspecting that inherited failure sheet before writing the required diagnosis; it rules out “repairing” bearing by recomputing a new angle convention.

The diagnosis is recorded before the policy edit, as required. I’m now making the single candidate a controlled continuation of the best sampled policy: only the behind-target bearing fraction changes from `-0.25` to `-0.50`; the target-ahead gait, guards, damping, steering limit, and transition scale stay fixed.

The durable guidance now incorporates both reusable results: the `-0.25` terminal fraction’s positive gradient and load boundary, plus the inherited full-circle-angle failure and the explicit warning against assuming an equivalent sign convention. I’m checking the final diff and then invoking the prescribed runner; no CFD will be run.

The prescribed guidance check found the same rendered-workspace metadata defect seen in the inherited parent: the assigned optimizer is marked twice as “copied to guidance,” so the checker cannot resolve a unique parent. I’m removing only the duplicate marker from the second listing, then rerunning the check; this does not alter task evidence or the solver candidate.

The policy check itself has not run because this shell’s login profile does not put Julia on `PATH`; the preceding SSH-profile warnings are unrelated. I’ll locate the already-installed Julia binary within the workspace environment and rerun the exact lightweight contract command with it, then run the boundary check.
